newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer says German economy picking up speed.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says German economy picking up speed.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said first quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) figures showed that the Germany economy was picking up speed and was on its way to meeting the targets set by the government in its annual economic report.
Data released on Thursday showed that Germany's GDP rose 1.4 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of 1997.
Tietmeyer also said it was critical that investments begin to play a bigger role in the German economy.

"The figures show a cyclical recovery in the first quarter. But now the issue is that the momentum becomes self-sustaining and above all that investments play a bigger role. This is the decisive point,"
Tietmeyer said he had no comments on Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
